body:
> **Decomposed 2026-09-01 into three children (below), all downstream of #255.** This body is now the
> brief for the root's own attempt — the verify-and-synthesize pass after every child has closed. The
> original design is preserved under *Design record* at the bottom: it is what each child was given.

## Why

Three PRs built the capability map, each reviewed on its own. Nobody has checked that the pieces fit, and no child
could write the documentation describing the whole.

## What

You are the root of a track. Your blockers' results arrive under **Parent task results**, but only for
the leaves you are directly blocked by — so read the others yourself before you start:

```
hkb show 259
hkb show 260
hkb show 261
hkb show 255   # the shared seam both this track and its sibling track depend on
```

**Do not redo their work.** Your job is the seam and the story:

1. **Run it for real** against this board and say what you saw.
2. **Check the pieces agree**: the exported vocabulary against what the docs and the brief claim, and
   every derived grant against `effectiveTools` (#255) rather than a second computation.
3. **Check the promise that nothing changes for a board that declares nothing** still holds end to end —
   it is asserted per child, and the whole is where it actually has to be true.
4. **Write what no child could**: the wiki page for the feature as one thing, and a `docs/wiki/log.md` entry.
5. **Report the gaps you did not fix** in your summary, as cards to file rather than silent edits.

## Done when

- [ ] The feature runs end to end on this board, described in the summary from what you actually saw.
- [ ] Every derived grant goes through `effectiveTools`; nothing computes a second answer.
- [ ] A board declaring nothing is byte-identically unchanged, verified across all three children.
- [ ] One wiki page describes the feature as a whole; `wiki-check.mjs` is clean for it.
- [ ] `npm run lint && npm test && npm run smoke` pass.

---

# Design record

*The original card, unchanged. The children above are how it was cut.*

> Found operating this board on 2026-09-01. The operator noticed a review being done by hand and asked why the
> harness's own review capability was not used — "a card with a goal should trigger the `/goal` of Claude Code
> if present". The board has no way to express that.

## Why

hkb knows how to *start* a session and nothing about what to reach for once inside it. A profile
(`DEFAULT_PROFILES`, `src/board.js:68`) carries `mode`, `launch`, `allowed_tools`, `model`, `effort`,
`heartbeat`, `max_in_progress`, `track`, `track_agents` — every one of them about spawning. Nothing maps a
*kind of work* to *the thing this harness does for that kind of work*.

There is exactly one half-attempt at it, and it is broken. `kb.skills` is a card field, and `src/context.js:132`
renders it into the worker brief:

```js
if (task.kb.skills?.length) lines.push(`Skills to apply: ${task.kb.skills.map((s) => '`/' + s + '`').join(', ')}\n`);
```

But `Skill` is not in `CLAUDE_TOOLS` and workers launch `--permission-mode dontAsk`, which **denies** an unlisted
tool rather than prompting — so the field instructs the worker to do something it is guaranteed to be refused.
That is #114. The reason it happened is the one this card is about: the field names a capability, and nothing
connects a named capability to the launch that would have to grant it.

The same hole shows up in three more places:

- **The operator seat's review step.** `/kanban:operate`'s `review` row says "read the PR against the card's
  *Done when*, run the repo's own checks" — prose. A harness with a real review capability (Claude Code's
  `/code-review`) is never told to use it, so whether a review is a skim or a systematic pass depends on what
  the session happens to think of. Observed today: four PRs reviewed by hand against *Done when*, which answers
  "does this meet the card" but not "what is wrong with this that the card never mentioned".
- **`kb.goal`.** Every card has acceptance criteria and `hkb context` prints them under a heading. A harness with
  a goal-tracking command never learns they exist.
- **`/kanban:specify` and `/kanban:decompose`** are Claude Code slash commands that Copilot and Codex reach only
  as skill sections read by name — the same mapping problem, already solved once, by hand, for those two.

Value 1 is portable: the protocol is labels, dependencies, refs and comments, and any harness drives it. So the
fix cannot be hkb calling `/code-review` — that is a harness-ism in the protocol exactly the way a `gh issue`
call would be a GitHub-ism. What is portable is the *intent*; only the binding is harness-specific.

## What

- **A capability map on the profile**, in `.kanban/board.json`, next to `allowed_tools`:

  ```json
  "claude": {
    "capabilities": { "review": "/code-review", "goal": "/goal", "specify": "/kanban:specify" }
  }
  ```

  The board names an intent from a small closed vocabulary; the profile says what this harness calls it. Export
  the vocabulary (`CAPABILITIES`) from `src/model.js` and pin it with a test the way `EVENT_KINDS` and
  `GROOM_KINDS` are pinned, so a new intent cannot be added without saying what it means.
- **No mapping is not an error.** A profile with no entry for an intent falls back to today's behaviour: the
  brief says what to achieve in prose. That is what keeps a Copilot or Codex board working unchanged, and it is
  the difference between a capability map and a dependency.
- **The map drives the launch, not just the prose.** This is the part that makes #114 a special case rather
  than a separate fix: if a profile maps an intent to something invoked with `Skill`, then `Skill` belongs in
  that launch's `allowed_tools`. Deriving the grant from the map is the only way the two cannot drift —
  #114 exists precisely because they did.
- **The operator seat is in scope.** `/kanban:operate`'s `review` row should say: run the profile's `review`
  capability if the board declares one, then judge against *Done when* — not one or the other. A session that
  reviews by hand where a capability exists is leaving the harness's own tooling on the table.
- **`hkb doctor`** prints each profile's capability map and flags an intent whose binding the launch cannot
  actually grant — the check #114 asks for, generalised.
- Pure resolution in `src/model.js` (`capabilityFor(cfg, profile, intent)`), rendering in `src/context.js`,
  schema and validation in `src/board.js`.

**Relationship to #114:** if this lands, #114's fix falls out of it — the `Skill` grant is derived rather than
hardcoded, and doctor's warning is the general one. Worth deciding whether #114 is superseded or stays as the
cheap fix to ship first; both are defensible and it is not this card's call.

## Done when

- [ ] A board can declare `capabilities` on a profile and a worker's brief names the bound command for every
      intent the card triggers; a profile with no mapping produces today's prose and no error.
- [ ] The vocabulary is exported from `src/model.js` and pinned by a test, as `EVENT_KINDS` is.
- [ ] A capability bound to a `Skill`-invoked command is reflected in that launch's `allowed_tools`, derived
      rather than duplicated, with a test that the two cannot drift.
- [ ] `hkb doctor` prints the map and flags a binding the launch cannot grant.
- [ ] `/kanban:operate`'s review row tells the seat to use the board's `review` capability when one is declared.
- [ ] `npm run lint && npm test` pass; a wiki page covers the map and its portability contract.
goal: A profile can declare a capability map binding a closed vocabulary of intents to this harness's commands; the brief names the bound command, an unmapped intent falls back to prose with no error, the Skill grant is derived from the map rather than duplicated, doctor flags a binding the launch cannot grant, and the operate review row uses the declared review capability
title: A profile knows how to start a session but nothing about what to reach for inside it, so kb.skills instructs a worker to use a tool the launch denies
